title: ledger: plain Verify (evolve ledger verify without --deep) fails on any sealed ledger, so evolve ledger anchor exits 2 after a seal
summary: Found by comment-reduction batch 22 (2026-09-26) and confirmed with a throwaway test run through -overlay; no file was changed. Once a ledger has been sealed, its first live line chains from a line that now lives in a sealed segment. Plain Verify stops at line 0 with 'chained-genesis prev_hash mismatch'; only VerifyDeep passes. `evolve ledger verify` without --deep therefore reports a healthy sealed ledger as broken. `evolve ledger anchor` runs plain Verify after recording, so it records the anchor and then exits 2. Also: TestVerify_DuplicatePrevHash never exercises duplicate detection (its duplicate is accepted as a fork sibling), no test drives two concurrent Seals, and ledger_test.go copies ZeroSeed as zero64.
fix: Make plain Verify start from the latest seal's anchor: take the sealed segment's tail hash as the expected prev_hash of the first live line, so a sealed ledger verifies without --deep. Test that seals and then runs plain Verify and anchor. Rename or rewrite the duplicate test, add a concurrent-Seal test, and use ZeroSeed.
acceptance: Plain Verify passes on a sealed, untampered ledger and fails on a tampered live line (tests)
evolve ledger anchor exits 0 after a seal (test)
Two concurrent Seals never both anchor the same segment (test)
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: The first seal, the only remedy for a 45.8 MB ledger, would make a healthy ledger read BROKEN and silently switch off the audit carry.
